title: TeraWulf Doubles Kentucky Data Center Power to 1 GW
key_facts: TeraWulf said on 5 Oct 2026 it doubled contracted electric service for its planned Muskie Data Campus in eastern Kentucky from 500 MW to 1 GW.
The second 500 MW phase moves up from 2030 to 2029; the first phase still starts ramping up in 2028.
The additional service needs Kentucky Public Service Commission approval.
Kentucky Power, an American Electric Power subsidiary, plans a new 765-kV substation and new 765-kV and 345-kV lines, targeted for service in October 2028; routes are not final.

If regulators approve, TeraWulf would fund about $100 million of winter bill credits for residential customers over 10 years and cover financing costs tied to a proposed 760-MW gas plant at Big Sandy.
No tenant has been announced for Muskie; TeraWulf is still weighing expansion to 2 GW.
Residents have questioned whether costs could rise for existing customers; Kentucky Power is taking public comments to 29 Oct.
quote_evidence: TeraWulf doubled contracted electric service for its Muskie Data Campus from 500 MW to 1 GW, with the second 500-MW phase advancing from 2030 to 2029.
The additional service is subject to Kentucky Public Service Commission approval and Kentucky Power's construction schedule.
The developer and operator of large-scale AI and high-performance computing data centers has not yet announced a tenant for Muskie.
why_it_matters_hint: A data center developer offers bill credits and cost sharing as it doubles its power order in a community worried about electricity bills.
notes: Announced 5 Oct 2026, reported 6 Oct inside the scan window.
